### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **22** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/dashboard.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/dashboard.md`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/view.md`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via diffItem (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.diffItem, bound to GET /api/v1/meta/:type/:name/diff), meta.diffItem (sdk, the route ledger binds it to GET /api/v1/meta/:type/:name/diff, selected by route anchor /:type/:name/diff))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via validateCapabilityReferences (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/permissions/capabilities.mdx`  _(via validateCapabilityReferences (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx`  _(via validateCapabilityReferences (symbol, a top-level function))_

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via RestServer (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v12.mdx`  _(via RestServer (symbol, a top-level class))_

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via RestServer (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via RestServer (symbol, a top-level class), /:type/:name/diff (route, bridged from symbol gatesOnItsOwnKey — its route source's handler names it; bridged from symbol gatesPerCaller — its route source's handler names it))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/dashboard.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/dashboard.md`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/view.md`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 31 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **145** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a360cee92e2eff7dda2f3e5a2baf8dfd013d77b7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4c4053f7650be25a4f6616293939299bd12461de` — the merge of head `60a6d43dd1c5632b9fb3a2a994bb15c8074bd18d` into base `a360cee92e2eff7dda2f3e5a2baf8dfd013d77b7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4c4053f7650be25a4f6616293939299bd12461de && git checkout 4c4053f7650be25a4f6616293939299bd12461de
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a360cee92e2eff7dda2f3e5a2baf8dfd013d77b7 60a6d43dd1c5632b9fb3a2a994bb15c8074bd18d && git checkout -B drift-repro a360cee92e2eff7dda2f3e5a2baf8dfd013d77b7 && git merge --no-ff 60a6d43dd1c5632b9fb3a2a994bb15c8074bd18d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a360cee92e2eff7dda2f3e5a2baf8dfd013d77b7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a360cee92e2eff7dda2f3e5a2baf8dfd013d77b7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `60a6d43dd1c5632b9fb3a2a994bb15c8074bd18d`
Local-runs: none

Read at 2026-10-10T21:49Z: card #22639 (body and every comment, the seat's ACCEPT weighed as one more claim), the ruling of record `6095014058` on #22611 at its source, PR #22731 (body, 27-file list, net diff against `main` at the head), the check-runs on the head, and `origin/main` files through `git show` to judge what the diff changes. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**Public surface (the accept-set and export questions).**
- `MetaItemReadRefusal` gains the member `audience-permission` (`403`, `PERMISSION_DENIED`, message). The type is a named `export type` in the second re-export block of `packages/rest/src/index.ts`, and `packages/rest/package.json` publishes one entry (`.`), so the widening reaches the published `@objectstack/rest` surface. RIGHT, and a widening: a consumer that switches on `reason` with an exhaustive arm gains a case; one that falls through on status and code (the runtime's `gateMetaItemDocument` does exactly that) needs nothing. `RestServer.sendMetaReadRefusal` adds the case beside `app-permission` on the same emitter, so the envelope is the app arm's.
- The four new module exports (`holdsRequiredPermissions`, `filterViewForUser`, `filterObjectListViewsForUser`, `withheldListViewNames`) reach no published entry: neither export block of `packages/rest/src/index.ts` names them, the entry has no star re-export, and the entry takes only `RestServer`, `RestProtocol`, `MountedRoute` and `metaItemPackageBinding` from `rest-server.ts`. `@objectstack/runtime`'s entry re-exports from `@objectstack/rest` only `RestServer`, `RouteManager`, `RouteGroupBuilder`, `createRestApiPlugin` and two types. `@objectstack/lint` adds no export (`validateCapabilityReferences` was already on its entry). `@objectstack/spec`: `AUDIENCE_REQUIRED_PERMISSIONS_DESCRIPTION` is not on the `ui` barrel, so no api-surface change; no Zod shape moves, so the accept set is unchanged. RIGHT: the seat's reading that only the union widens holds.

**The describe and the two liveness rows.**
- `packages/spec/src/ui/audience-required-permissions.ts`: the `[PLANNED — not enforced yet]` clause and its sentence are gone; the replacement states the four things the diff enforces (not listed, refused by name, container entries pruned, an object's own list views pruned for a caller outside the D4 class). The marker removal is load-bearing (`markerStatus` grades a row-less property off `[planned`) and the spec pin now asserts no `[planned` and no `not enforced`, and still no tracker number. RIGHT. Precision note, not a defect: "a user who may not edit the object" is ADR-0106 D4's own shorthand; the class actually served whole is `isObjectSchemaMaskExempt`: `isSystem`, or a holder of `manage_metadata`, `studio.access` or `setup.access`.
- `liveness/view.json` `list.requiredPermissions` and `liveness/dashboard.json` `requiredPermissions`: `planned` to `live`, `authorWarn` and `authorHint` dropped, `evidenceScope: in-repo`, `evidence` cites `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts#holdsRequiredPermissions` plus the arms and the three pin files, and the note records the flip and its boundaries. The state-count shards move `planned` 1 to 0 and `live` up one per type. The two lint warn pins are re-subjected to silence beside a lit `object.externalSharingModel` control in the same call and assert the row's `status` and `evidence`. `Spec property liveness` on the head is success. RIGHT; none deleted.

**What each audience is served, per door the diff gates (read in the diff against `origin/main`).**
- ONE predicate. `holdsRequiredPermissions`: not an array, or empty, is no gate; every name must be held; the app arm's two inline `every` checks are replaced by it with identical semantics. No any-of form anywhere in the diff. RIGHT per letter A and triage's "one predicate" direction.
- `GET /meta/view` (list, both transports, the `?object=` switcher included): holder served all; non-holder: ONE gated view (a view item's `config`, or a flattened view's top level) dropped, a container served minus its gated `list` / `listViews` entries; a view naming no key served to all. The runtime list goes through `createMetaListAnswer`, which calls `createMetaListReadGate`, so the dispatcher rides the same arm. RIGHT.
- `GET /meta/view/NAME`: ONE gated view refused whole (`403 PERMISSION_DENIED`) on every door, author or not; a container pruned, except on the four stored-version doors for a `mayWriteItem` caller (set from `metaSaveVerdict(caller).allowed` on `RestServer` and from the `PUT` branch's own admission on the dispatcher, type-generic on both). The census's `AUTHOR_EXEMPTION.types` becomes `['app', 'view']` and the predicate is pinned against `PUT /meta/view/clm_contract`. RIGHT, the app arm's two rules carried over.
- The CACHED arm. On `origin/main` the default plain read excludes only app, dashboard, draft, preview, package-scoped, book and doc from `getMetaItemCached`, so `view` and `object` take it; the diff gates both there with the same judge (`arms: 'all'`, `app: 'gate'`), hands the protocol no `If-None-Match` for them, folds `withheldListViewNames` into the validator and judges `304` locally. `foldVisibilityFingerprintIntoEtag` returns the ETag unchanged on an empty fingerprint, so nothing withheld leaves the validator as before. RIGHT; without this the ruling's by-name read would have stayed ungated on the default path.
- `GET /meta/dashboard` and by-name: audience first, under both `arms`, then the ADR-0057 D10 widget gate under `arms: 'all'` only; dashboards never take the cached arm. `gatesPerCaller` now answers true for `view` and `dashboard`, so `/history`, `/audit` and `/diff` fetch and judge the current document. RIGHT; a dashboard's direct URL is refused by the server, as the ruling asks.
- `GET /meta/object` and by-name (both arms, the cached arm, the dispatcher's protocol, metadata and ObjectQL-registry exits, and the legacy one-segment exit): `listViews` pruned for every caller outside the D4 class; whole for the D4 class on every door (a pruned load PUT back would delete the withheld entries, the rule the field mask already holds). `gatesPerCaller('object')` stays false, and that is RIGHT: the three doors that ask it each call `refuseNonAuthoringCaller`, whose predicate is `mayReadPendingDrafts`, a bare delegation to `isObjectSchemaMaskExempt`, so no caller the arm would prune ever reaches them.
- Caller classes. ANONYMOUS: every audience arm serves a caller with no `userId` ungated (`callerSystemPermissions` answers null, the app arm's standing rule). Upstream-guarded, not a hole: `RestServer`'s `/meta` wrapper lets an unresolved caller past `enforceAuth` only for `isPublicAudienceRead` (GET, book or doc list or item, or the book tree); the dispatcher answers `anonymousDeny()` unless the same predicate admits; `shouldDenyAnonymous` is false only for a `userId`, `isSystem`, or an allow-listed path. The census pins `anonymous` refused `401` on every subject and door, and the parity files hold the dispatcher equal. SYSTEM caller (`isSystem`, no user): served ungated by every arm, as the app arm and the D4 class already serve it; not a user audience, not new. AUTHOR (`mayWriteItem`): as above. D4-EXEMPT on the object door: a `studio.access` or `setup.access` holder reads an object's gated `listViews` whole while `/meta/view/OBJECT.KEY` refuses them by name. Judged RIGHT under ADR-0106 D4 and stated in the PR, the liveness note and the docs; the console's `useServedViewItems` merges `/meta/object` list views with `/meta/view` documents, so a Studio-class non-holder may be shown an entry whose by-name read refuses. That is the objectui half the card files after acceptance; naming it here for that filing.
- A door outside `/meta`, checked: `GET /api/v1/ui/view/:object/:type` delegates to the protocol's `getUiView`, which synthesises a default grid or form from the object's fields and reads no `listViews` entry and no `/meta/view` document, so no `requiredPermissions` carrier is served there. Not a hole for this key.
- `/diff`, `/history`, `/audit` of a NEVER-published gated view or dashboard: served as before (no current document to judge), to the authoring class only, which reads the same draft body through `GET /meta/_drafts` on every type. A stated boundary of the existing draft-door rule, not a hole the ruling's list read or by-name read opens.
- The lint: `validateCapabilityReferences` resolves a dashboard, a container's `list` and each `listViews` entry, a view item's `config`, a flattened view's top level and an object's own `listViews`, each at its own path, warning severity like every other carrier, with a lit control. RIGHT. The docs callout in `capabilities.mdx` now claims exactly what is enforced; the references are regenerated.
- Check-runs on the head as read at the stamp above: success for Build Core, Build Docs, Check Changeset (three runs), Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate (the aggregate and all three shards), Dogfood Verify CLI, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, No other open PR may claim the same issue, No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path, Part-of PR must not also close its card, Spec property liveness, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Test Core (2/6) and (5/6), The card this PR closes must claim this branch, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates, filter, Auto Label; still in progress: Test Core shards 1, 3, 4 and 6, Lint & Repo Gates, Type Check · workspace. Console Pin Gate and the opt-in tarball smoke are skipped. No failure read. The landing still waits on every required context being success, as the ACCEPT says.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/rest` **minor**: RIGHT. A published type union widens and the server gains behaviour.
- `@objectstack/lint` **minor**: RIGHT. New warnings at six positions on an exported function, additive.
- `@objectstack/runtime` **patch**: RIGHT. One ungated exit now asks the shared gate; the runtime entry publishes no refusal type and no export moves.
- `@objectstack/spec` **patch**: RIGHT. Describe prose, two ledger rows and regenerated references; Zod shape and accept set unchanged; the description constant is on no barrel. The key itself is still unreleased on `main` (`.changeset/22611-list-view-dashboard-required-permissions.md` is present; spec and rest sit at 17.7.0), so enforcing it narrows no released accept set: the gate withholds only documents carrying a key no release has yet accepted.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body's second line and in the rest changeset: RIGHT. The one published-contract change is the union widening; the other three changesets carry `Clause-②: no`; the three `Check Changeset` runs on the head are success.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report `6102380489`, each deviation:
1. File surface past the claim (`packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts`): ANSWERED. Both packages are in the `domain:cli` lane (`references/lanes/cli.md`), the cached arm is the default by-name read the ruling names, and the legacy object exit was the one object door that served the schema through the mask alone. `metadata-core` stays untouched on a measured reason (the FLS walk judges only the denied-field set under a `project` posture; gating there would be a second evaluator). Accepted.
2. Type surface: ANSWERED in ① and ②; the seat re-declared the card and the PR line to `yes (widening)` and graded rest `minor`. Accepted.
3. `/diff` of a never-published view or dashboard served ungated: ANSWERED in ①; accepted as the stated boundary (the alternative, absence, would turn every draft-only view's diff into `404`, pinned by `meta-history-diff-authoring-door.test.ts`). Note for the release compiler, carrier the release compiler: the rest changeset's sentence that every alternate door, `/diff`, `/history` and `/audit` named, refuses the item holds for a published gated item; the never-published case is served to the authoring class and is stated in the PR body, not in the changeset. Not a defect; the compile reads both texts.
4. Five pins re-subjected (the census edge and two runtime parity controls to `flow`, keeping the no-key `view` control as "no key served to all"; two `/audit` stubs to `reports`): ANSWERED. Read in the diff, each carries its reason, none deleted. Accepted.
5. Spec suite in three shards: procedural; CI's `Test Core` shards are the record. Accepted.

`out_of_scope_findings`, each:
1. `packages/spec/liveness/README.md` view and dashboard state-table notes still describe the key as planned with `authorWarn`: ESCALATED as a note to the `domain:spec` seat (the dev's carrier); drift outside this card's three named spec files, not a defect class; no gate reads it (`Spec property liveness` is success).
2. `packages/spec/src/system/metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts` omit rows' `why` text says "not enforced yet": ESCALATED as a note to the `domain:spec` seat; whether the Studio forms offer the key is the ruling that text names, not this card's; the pin is green.
3. `.changeset/22611-list-view-dashboard-required-permissions.md` says "Not enforced yet" and will ship beside this PR's four changesets if both land in one release: NOTED for the release compiler, which compiles release notes centrally from the changesets and reads the later sentence; no code PR edits another card's changeset.

The ACCEPT's open ask (anonymous callers): CONFIRMED in ①, upstream-guarded on both transports.
